findings.title: FamousSparrow: A suspicious hotel guest
findings.summary_md: ESET researchers documented FamousSparrow, a China-aligned APT active since at least 2019 that exploited the ProxyLogon vulnerability and targeted hotels, governments, and private companies worldwide. The group is the original and, at the time, only known user of the SparrowDoor backdoor. This is the earliest public anchor for the Sparrow toolset later attributed to the CopperDragon quartermaster.

findings.title: Mélofée: a new alien malware in the Panda's toolset targeting Linux hosts
findings.summary_md: ExaTrack discovered Mélofée, a previously undocumented Linux implant and kernel rootkit family targeting Linux servers, linked with high confidence to Chinese state-sponsored APT groups. Check Point Research later connected Melofee to CopperDragon's SparrowShell through shared Reptile rootkit code and reused self-signed certificates. This establishes the Linux side of the framework years before the CopperDragon report.

findings.title: New malicious web shell from the Tropic Trooper group is found in the Middle East
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky identified Tropic Trooper delivering CrowDoor, a variant of the SparrowDoor backdoor first documented by ESET in September 2021, through DLL search-order hijacking against a government entity in the Middle East. The finding places TropicTrooper among the consumers of the Sparrow toolset well before the CopperDragon framework was named. CrowDoor traces its lineage back to SparrowDoor, which Check Point later folds into the CopperDragon ecosystem.

findings.title: You will always remember this as the day you finally caught FamousSparrow
findings.summary_md: ESET documented FamousSparrow intrusions dating to July 2024, including two previously undocumented SparrowDoor variants and the group's first observed use of a keylogger. The report confirms continued evolution of the Sparrow toolset by the same operator. It predates the CopperDragon attribution by roughly eight months.

findings.title: UAT-9244 targets South American telecommunication providers with three new malware implants
findings.summary_md: Cisco Talos disclosed UAT-9244, a China-nexus APT assessed with high confidence to overlap with FamousSparrow and Tropic Trooper, targeting South American telecommunications providers with TernDoor, PeerTime, and BruteEntry. TernDoor derives from CrowDoor and, by extension, SparrowDoor. The report establishes both the telecom victimology and the Sparrow lineage before the CopperDragon publication.

findings.title: Beware the SparroWock: The backdoor that bites, the commands that catch
findings.summary_md: ESET researchers documented SparroWocky, FamousSparrow's new flagship backdoor that replaced SparrowDoor and has been deployed in Latin America since at least August 2025 against government organizations. Check Point Research later identified the same implant as CopperDoor and linked it to the DarkWire cluster. This is the most recent pre-existing reporting on the framework before the CopperDragon publication.
